title: Not Your Keys: Getting Started in Crypto

cards.aki: Let's set you up with the basics everyone else pretends to know.
cards.title: Not Your Keys
text: Wallets, coins and tokens, stablecoins, exchanges, swaps, fees, blockchains, and what perps and options are.
Six minutes, then a quick quiz for your certificate.

cards.title: Wallets
text: A wallet does not hold coins. It holds the keys that prove the coins on the blockchain are yours. Tap each tile.

items.back: An app or browser extension, like MetaMask or Phantom. Handy for everyday use, and online all the time.
A small device, like a Ledger or Trezor, that keeps your keys offline. Safer for savings.
12 or 24 words that can rebuild your wallet anywhere. Whoever has them owns everything in it. Write them on paper, never share them.
When crypto sits on an exchange, the exchange holds the keys for you. People say: not your keys, not your coins.

cards.aki: This one matters more than anything else today.
cards.title: Someone in a chat offers to fix your wallet if you share your seed phrase. What do you do?

options.text: Share it, they are from support
options.why: Real support never asks for your seed phrase. Anyone who does is trying to empty your wallet.

options.text: Never share it, and block them
options.why: Exactly. Your seed phrase is your money. No one else ever needs it.

options.text: Share only half of the words
options.why: Even part of it helps a thief. Never share any of it.

cards.aki: Coins, tokens, stablecoins: same thing? Not quite.
cards.title: Coins, tokens and stablecoins
points: A coin is the main currency of its own blockchain, like BTC on Bitcoin, ETH on Ethereum or SOL on Solana.
A token is built on top of a blockchain, like a project's token on Ethereum.
A stablecoin is a token designed to stay worth one dollar, like USDT or USDC. They are how most people move money in crypto.
cards.tip: Stablecoins can lose their dollar link. In 2022 a big one called UST collapsed to almost zero. Stick to large, well-known ones and spread the risk.

cards.aki: Different blockchains are like different countries.
cards.title: Blockchains
text: Each blockchain is its own network, with its own coin used to pay fees. Tap to compare a few.

items.back: The first one. Built for sending and holding bitcoin. Slow and very secure.
The home of smart contracts, DeFi and NFTs. Fees are paid in ETH.
A fast, cheap network popular for trading and memecoins. Fees are paid in SOL.
Networks like Base and Arbitrum that sit on top of Ethereum to make it faster and cheaper.

cards.aki: Now, where people actually buy and sell.
cards.title: CEX and DEX

items.back: A centralised exchange, run by a company, like Binance, Coinbase or Kraken. You sign up with ID, deposit money and the exchange holds your crypto.
A decentralised exchange, like Uniswap or Jupiter. Smart contracts swap tokens straight from your own wallet. No sign up.
Easy, with card and bank payments. But you trust the company, and exchanges have failed before.
You stay in control of your coins. But anyone can list a token, including scams, and mistakes cannot be undone.

cards.aki: Here is what happens when you swap on a DEX.
cards.title: How a swap works

steps.label: 1. Connect your wallet
steps.text: Open the DEX from its real address, then connect your wallet. Bookmark it so you never land on a fake copy.

steps.label: 2. Pick the tokens
steps.text: Choose what you give and what you get. Check the token's contract address, since scammers copy popular names.

steps.label: 3. Check the price
steps.text: Look at price impact and slippage: how much worse your price can get while the trade goes through.

steps.label: 4. Approve and confirm
steps.text: Your wallet asks you to approve and sign. You pay a network fee, called gas, and the tokens arrive in seconds.

cards.title: The fees you will meet
points: Gas: the network fee for every transaction, paid in that chain's coin.
Trading fee: what an exchange or DEX charges per trade.
Spread: the gap between the buy and sell price.
Slippage: the price moving against you while a trade goes through.
Withdrawal fee: what an exchange charges to send crypto out.
cards.tip: Always keep a little of the chain's coin, like ETH or SOL, in your wallet to pay gas.

cards.aki: A classic beginner mistake. What would you do?
cards.title: You want to send USDT to a friend. What must match on both sides?

options.why: Wallet colours do not matter at all.

options.text: The network, like Ethereum or Solana
options.why: Yes. USDT exists on many networks. Send on a different network than your friend's address and the money can be lost.
Crypto works around the clock. The network is what matters.

cards.aki: You will hear about these everywhere. Here is the short version.
cards.title: Perps and options

items.back: Perpetual futures: bets on a price going up or down, with no end date. Usually traded with borrowed money.
Borrowed money that multiplies gains and losses. At 10x, a 10 percent move against you can wipe out your whole stake.
When your losses hit the limit, the exchange closes your position and your money is gone.
The right, but not the duty, to buy or sell at a set price before a set date. Powerful and complex.

cards.tip: Perps and options are advanced tools. Most beginners who trade them lose money. Learn first, trade later, if at all.

cards.aki: You now know more than most people on your timeline.
cards.title: Quick recap
points: Wallets hold keys, and your seed phrase is your money. Never share it.
Coins run blockchains, tokens live on them, stablecoins track the dollar.
CEX: easy, but a company holds your coins. DEX: you hold them, and you must be careful.
Watch gas, trading fees, spread and slippage, and always match the network.
Perps and options use leverage. Leave them for later.
